subject: Streaming SLA matrix & pilot owners — clarifications and next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Li <morgan.li@nebulas.ai>, Avery Singh <avery@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming SLA matrix & pilot owners — clarifications and next steps

Hi Morgan / Avery —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. I wanted to capture the performance-related commitments and flag open questions so we can lock the pilot scope. I attached an initial SLA matrix (SLA_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a mutual action plan draft (Nebulas_MAP_v0.3.docx) — both are pointers, not final.

Summary of what we observed and what you asked for during the call:
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 200 ms for text-generation API (streaming token-by-token preferred)
- Throughput: sustained baseline of ~150 req/s with burst to 250 req/s for peak windows
- Concurrency: expect ~40 concurrent active sessions (chat-style) during busy hours
- Streaming requirement: token emission latency goal <= 60 ms from model output to client (we discussed delta between chunked vs token-by-token)

Open clarifications we need from you to finalize the pilot agreement:
1) Confirm the p95 latency and whether 200 ms is an absolute SLO or a pilot acceptance threshold.
2) Identify the canonical test prompt set we should use for pilot traffic (we can host a secure shared Drive folder).
3) Will Nebulas require end-to-end encryption at rest with customer KMS for the pilot? (This affects Private deployment timeline.)
4) Expected duration for pilot (30, 60, 90 days) and success criteria beyond raw numbers (eg: quality regression tolerance, error budget policy).

Proposed owners / next steps (high-level):
- Redwood: Ben Carter (PS Engineering) — pilot infra config, telemetry plan, canary policy
- Redwood: Jonas Weber (SE) — SLO matrix finalization and kickoff call
- Nebulas: Morgan Li — product/ops owner to approve test traffic & timelines

Target: get agreement on SLO matrix + MAP by EOD Friday (2028-05-18) so we can provision a dedicated pilot pool the week of 5/22.

Please reply with confirmations or edits inline — I’ll consolidate and send a final MAP.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jonas.weber@redwood.com]

[Attachment: SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: Nebulas_MAP_v0.3.docx (docx)]

From: Morgan Li <morgan.li@nebulas.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Avery Singh <avery@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming SLA matrix & pilot owners — clarifications and next steps

Thanks Jonas — solid summary. A few quick clarifications from our side after syncing with infra and product: 

- Latency: we can accept 200 ms p95 as a pilot acceptance threshold, but our long-term target is 150 ms p95. For the pilot, please mark 200 ms as the acceptance bar and 150 ms as stretch.
- Throughput: baseline 150 req/s is correct. We will likely need bursts to 300 req/s for short windows during batch sends — can Redwood support a 2x burst policy?
- Concurrency: 40 active sessions is average; peak concurrency could hit 65 during marketing spikes. We need graceful degradation — not hard failure at 65.
- Streaming: we prefer token-by-token streaming. Token-sent latency target is 50 ms if achievable; we recognize model/infra constraints.
- KMS: For the initial pilot, Nebulas can use Redwood-hosted KMS; if pilot is successful we will require customer-managed KMS for production.
- Pilot length: let's start with a 45-day pilot (recommended by ops) with a go/no-go checkpoint at day 21.

Telemetry / acceptance artifacts we need from Redwood for the pilot:
1) Per-request p50/p95/p99 latency breakdowns (endpoint + network + token-emit split)
2) Per-shard throughput and queue-length metrics for the dedicated pool
3) Error-rate and partial-response counts for streaming sessions
4) Example payloads / canonical prompt set for reproducible tests

We can provide the canonical prompt set — I’ll drop it in the Drive link you suggested. Regarding the 2x burst, could Ben confirm whether autoscale + burst capacity can cover 300 req/s for short windows and whether that affects cost transparency?

Cheers,
Morgan Li
Head of Product Operations, Nebulas.ai
[morgan.li@nebulas.ai]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Morgan Li <morgan.li@nebulas.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Streaming SLA matrix & pilot owners — clarifications and next steps

Morgan —

Thanks for the clear priorities. Quick technical notes and how Redwood will map them into the pilot: 

1) Burst capacity: we can support a 2x burst policy with a short-lived burst buffer backed by autoscaling GPUs. We’ll size the burst pool for 300 req/s sustained for 2-minute windows, with autoscale cooldowns. This will be visible on telemetry and billed separately as burst usage in the MAP.

2) Concurrency and graceful degradation: we’ll configure request-level queuing with prioritized traffic for interactive sessions. Above the concurrency threshold we will return token-streamed partial responses with a degradation policy (reduce model context length and route to quantized variant) rather than hard failures.

3) Streaming token latency: token-by-token is supported. The main determinants will be model variant, backend kernel path, and network hop to your region. For pilot we’ll instrument token-emit latency and provide a per-token histogram in dashboards. Achieving 50 ms is reasonable for many model/sequence-length pairs, but we’ll validate with your canonical prompts.

4) Telemetry: we’ll export p50/p95/p99 plus token-emission split, per-shard throughput, queue length, and error-rate. We propose to use a shared Kibana/console dashboard and to provide sample raw traces for 7 days as acceptance evidence.

Action items I’ll own:
- Provide a revised SLA_matrix with explicit definitions (p95 measurement windows, warm vs cold starts) by EOD Thu (2028-05-16).
- Deliver telemetry dashboard link + sample traces for a synthetic run by Tue (2028-05-21).
- Cost overlay for burst usage and dedicated pool sizing by Fri (2028-05-18).

Jonas / Grace: if you can confirm the Drive prompt set and Morgan confirms the day-21 checkpoint criteria, we’ll begin provisioning.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[ben.carter@redwood.com]

Subject: Re: Streaming SLA matrix & pilot owners — clarifications and next steps

Morgan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear acceptance framing. I’ve updated the MAP with the day-21 checkpoint and stretch goals; Ben’s working the SLA_matrix edits and the cost overlay.

Agreed next steps and owners (finalized):
- Nebulas (Morgan): approve canonical prompt set and confirm day-21 go/no-go criteria (due 2028-05-18)
- Redwood (Ben): updated SLA_matrix + cost overlay + telemetry dashboard (due 2028-05-18)
- Redwood (Jonas): schedule pilot kickoff and produce a short runbook showing how we’ll generate synthetic traffic for the day-0 baseline (targeting 2028-05-22 provisioning)

I’ll send a calendar invite for Monday 5/22 09:00 PDT for the kickoff unless you request another time. If Nebulas is comfortable, please sign the MAP doc and reply with a PO to unblock provisioning — otherwise we’ll provision a smaller test pool that does not require a PO.

HubSpot: HS-238742 — I’ll update the stage to 'Pilot: provisioning' once we have the signed MAP.

Thanks again — we’ll aim to have the telemetry dashboard and initial synthetic traces available by 2028-05-21.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jonas.weber@redwood.com]
